questions.question: Do ranker blends survive staged racing better than the raw linear ranker?
questions.why: Tests whether a tiny readable prior fixes imitation-policy weakness without leaving the public DecisionFrame boundary.

questions.question: For a fixed MAP-Elites deck shell, which pilot family uses the construction best?
questions.why: Separates construction strength from pilot/controller strength.

questions.question: Are ranker policies failing because of the deck shell, the policy, or mulligan choice?
questions.why: The same deck can be paired with multiple pilots; future turns can add same-pilot multiple mulligan policies.

questions.question: Does sequential racing eliminate ranker candidates too aggressively under small samples?
questions.why: Stage decisions are visible and can be replayed with larger reps or wider intervals.

questions.question: Should the next learned policy be an MLP/listwise ranker or should we improve imitation data first?
questions.why: If blended linear rankers still underperform, data quality may matter more than model capacity.

questions.question: Can C++ batch trace checking remain zero-skip and zero-mismatch as policies diversify?
questions.why: C++ is useful only if new evaluation traffic stays inside audited transition coverage.

questions.question: Which MAP-Elites descriptor cells deserve larger budget?
questions.why: Use same-deck pilot summaries and staged races to spend games only on live construction regions.

questions.question: Should mulligan policy be the next learned subproblem?
questions.why: Bad mulligans contaminate every policy evaluation and are now agent-facing.
